sentences.text:

none appears for the respondents.
Perused the original record and proceedings.

3) It is the case of the appellant that on the day of accident, the appellant was going from Udaipur to Morbi in Truck No.GJ-12-T-7845 as a cleaner and driver of the said Truck was driving the said truck NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4828/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined rashly and negligently with an excessive speed, due to which the Truck dashed with the rock.
As a result, the appellant sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the appellant has filed MAC Petition seeking compensation.
After appreciating the evidence produced on record the learned Tribunal was pleased to partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.76,000/- against the claim of Rs.8,50,000/-.

4) Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the Tribunal has committed error in not considering future prospective income and therefore, ought to have considered the fact that the appellant was 46 years old, 25 % future prospective is required to be considered.
Also, the Tribunal has awarded meager amounts of Rs.10,000/- and Rs.5,000/- under the head of pain, shock and suffering and under the head of special diet and attendant charges respectively.
The Tribunal has also not properly assessed the income of the claimant as he was earning Rs.3,500/- p.m by doing cleaner work.
Even considering the minimum wage prevailing at the time of accident, he has requested to reassess the income of the appellant.
Hence, he has requested to enhance the compensation amount in the appeal.
5) Having considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the appellant and considering the material placed on record, it appears that the appeal is filed only on the aspect of quantum.
Hence, this appeal is required to be decided on the aspect of quantum only.
Alleged incident is not in dispute.
Involvement of the vehicle is also not in dispute.

In order to prove the claim, the claimant has filed an Affidavit at Exh:30, FIR at Exh:31, Panchnama of scene of incident at Exh:32, Disability certificate at Exhs:39 and 42 and medical bills at Exh:35.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4828/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined 6)

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC), that if no proof of income is produced on the record then Tribunal has to consider prevalent minimum wages in absence of ample evidence of monthly income of the appellant.

entities.text: Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the accident occurred in 2002 and during that time, as per the Government approved minimum wages was Rs.2,200/-, whereas, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the appellant as Rs.30,000/- per annum without producing any income proof, which is just and proper.

7) So far as disability is concerned, the appellant has produced a disability certificate at Exh:39 issued by Dr. Hemang Patel, wherein he has opined that the appellant was operated for DHS plate fixation for fracture upper end femur and he was treated as an indoor patient from 11.05.2002 to 20.05.2002 and has assessed disability to the tune of 33% of right lower limb.
However, both the parties agreed to assess the disability at 13% for the body as a whole.
Therefore, the Tribunal has Chhagangiri Shankargiri Goswami vs Devkaran Vasan Ayer on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183714740/

2 rightly assessed the disability to the extent of 13%.
8)

In the present case, the accident occurred in 2002 and during that time, the appellant - injured was clearer in truck and the Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured as Rs.30,000/- per annum which is just and proper.

As the Tribunal has considered multiplier of 13 as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
[2009 (6) SCC 121] which is also just and proper.

sentences.text:
Now if we reassess the compensation with reassessed income of the injured Rs.30,000/- p.a income on adding future prospects income at 25%,
then it would come to Rs.37,500/- p.a.

By applying 13 multiplier and deduction of 13 % NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4828/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/03/2026 undefined disability, it comes to Rs.63,375/- (37,500/- x 13 multiplier x 13% disability) under the head of future loss of income.

9) As the Tribunal has already awarded Rs.51,000/- towards future loss of income, the appellant is entitled to get additional amount of Rs.12,375/- under the head of future loss of income.
10) So far as other amount awarded under other conventional heads are concerned, the same are proper and do not require any interference.

11) As discussed above, the appellant is entitled to get compensation computed as under:
 Heads Awarded by Reassessed by  Tribunal  Pain, shock and Rs.10,000/- Rs.10  sufferings

Actual loss of Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,
 income  Medical expenditure Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,
 Transportation, Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,
 Special diet, and  attendant charges  Future loss of Rs.51,000/- Rs.63,
 income  Total Rs.76,000/- Rs.88,
 compensation  12)

In view of above, as the Tribunal has awarded total compe Rs.76,000/-, however, as discussed above the appellant would be entitled to get additional amount of Rs.12,375/- with proportionate costs and interest as awarded by the learned Tribunal.
13) Hence, present appeal is partly allowed.
